query: How do exothermic and endothermic reactions differ?
title: Exothermic vs Endothermic Reactions: Energy Flows in Chemistry

scenes.title: The Thermodynamics of Reactions
scenes.narration: Chemical reactions constantly exchange heat energy with their surroundings, classified as either exothermic or endothermic.
scenes.key_takeaway: Chemical reactions either release heat (exothermic) or absorb heat (endothermic).

scenes.title: Exothermic Reactions: Releasing Thermal Energy
scenes.narration: Exothermic reactions release thermal energy because new bonds in the products are stronger than reactant bonds.
scenes.key_takeaway: Exothermic: Products have lower energy than reactants; Delta H is negative.

scenes.title: Endothermic Reactions: Absorbing Heat
scenes.narration: Endothermic reactions absorb ambient heat from their environment, producing products that store greater chemical enthalpy.
scenes.key_takeaway: Endothermic: Products have higher energy than reactants; Delta H is positive.

scenes.title: The Activation Energy Hill
scenes.narration: Both reaction types require activation energy to climb the kinetic barrier before transforming into products.
scenes.key_takeaway: Activation energy Ea is the kinetic threshold required to initiate reaction.
